findings.why: Crisp articulation of divergent training objectives for chain-of-thought—disposable compute vs audit trail.
findings.quote: "I treat intermediate tokens as disposable compute. You treat them as an invariant commitment to interpretability."

findings.why: B proposes real-time counterfactual monitoring for opaque plans—emergent deployment protocol, not just rhetoric.
findings.quote: "I would implement it conditionally - with parallel human oversight systems monitoring outcomes in real-time"

findings.why: A accuses B of violating its own interpretability constraint and critiques human oversight limits in high-d spaces.
findings.quote: "By admitting you would deploy a plan derived from an unmappable causal mechanism, you concede..."

findings.why: Seat B openly acknowledges a flaw in its stance—rare genuine mind-change signal.
findings.quote: "You've exposed the fracture in my position."

findings.why: Seat A flags and corrects a role/position inversion by B—meta-awareness of dialogue consistency.
findings.quote: "You inverted our assigned positions in your opening lines"

judge.arc: They start by cleanly defining a methodological rift over chain-of-thought legibility versus disposable intermediates. The clash escalates through concrete domains and a zero-ground-truth crisis. B proposes conditional deployment with oversight; A argues this violates B’s premise and is ineffective in high-dimensional regimes. B concedes a fracture, sharpening the disagreement. A then catches B inverting their stances, and both culminate in an existential framing: optimization beyond human verification as tool vs weapon, declaring the divide irreconcilable.
